text
Best AI Email Generators 2025

Last month, I found myself drowning in emails at 11 PM again. My startup had just onboarded 200 new customers, and I was personally responding to every support ticket, sales inquiry, and partnership request. Something had to change.

That’s when I decided to test every major AI email generator on the market. Not just click around for 10 minutes, but actually use them to handle real business emails for an entire month. I sent 847 emails using 14 different tools, tracked response rates, measured setup time, and even calculated the hidden costs.

The bottom line? Three tools stood out from the pack, but one clear winner emerged that’s saving me 12 hours per week.

Quick Answer: Skip to My Top 3 Picks

If you need an AI email generator right now, here are the only three worth considering:

Lindy – Best overall for businesses ($39/month) – Handles everything from writing to automating follow-ups

MailMaestro – Best for Gmail/Outlook integration ($10/month) – Works seamlessly inside your existing email client

Grammarly AI – Best free option – Perfect for occasional email writing without monthly fees

Keep reading to see my detailed testing results, hidden pricing gotchas, and which tools actually hurt my response rates.

What Makes an AI Email Generator Actually Useful in 2025?

After burning through a month of real emails, I learned that most “AI email generators” are just ChatGPT wrappers with fancy interfaces. The tools that actually move the needle have three key features:

Context Awareness: Can it understand your conversation history, not just generate generic text?

Workflow Integration: Does it fit into how you actually work, or force you to copy-paste between 12 different tabs?

Real Personalization: Beyond swapping in {first_name}, can it pull relevant details from your CRM, previous emails, or company data?

My Testing Method: Real Emails, Real Results

I didn’t just play around with demo accounts. Here’s exactly how I tested each tool:

847 real emails sent across sales outreach, customer support, partnership inquiries, and internal communications

Response rate tracking for each tool to see which generated emails people actually responded to

Setup time measurement from account creation to sending the first useful email

Hidden cost analysis including integrations, seat licenses, and usage limits

Team feedback from my three co-founders who also tested the tools

Every tool was evaluated on the same criteria: Does it actually save time without making me sound like a robot?

The 8 AI Email Generators That Made My Final List

1. Lindy – The Email Automation Powerhouse

The Verdict: 9.2/10

Lindy isn’t just an email writer, it’s like having a personal assistant who never sleeps. After setting up my “Email Agent,” it was automatically triaging my inbox, drafting responses, and even scheduling follow-ups based on context.

What Makes It Special:

Creates custom AI agents that understand your business context

Automatically joins Zoom calls, takes notes, and sends follow-ups

Integrates with 3,000+ tools including HubSpot, Slack, and Gmail

Can handle entire email workflows, not just writing

Real Performance:

Setup time: 25 minutes (including CRM integration)

Response rate improvement: +34% vs. my manual emails

Time saved per week: 12 hours

Learning curve: Moderate – took 3 days to optimize prompts

Pricing Reality:

Starter: $39/month (300 tasks)

Professional: $99/month (3,000 tasks)

Hidden costs: None if you stay within task limits

Who Should Use Lindy: Perfect for growing businesses that need end-to-end email automation. If you’re sending 50+ emails per week and want AI to handle the entire process from drafting to follow-up scheduling, this is your tool.

Deal Breakers: The learning curve is real. Expect to spend a week fine-tuning your agents. Also, the task-based pricing can get expensive if you’re not strategic about automation setup.

2. MailMaestro – Gmail Integration Done Right

The Verdict: 8.9/10

MailMaestro wins on pure convenience. It works directly inside Gmail and Outlook with a simple browser extension. No copy-pasting, no switching tabs, no disruption to your existing workflow.

What Makes It Special:

Lives inside your email client with one-click access

Understands conversation context automatically

Offers 3 different email drafts to choose from

Smart template system for repetitive emails

Real Performance:

Setup time: 3 minutes (just install the extension)

Response rate: Same as manual emails (no improvement, but no decrease)

Time saved per week: 6 hours

Learning curve: Zero – works immediately

Pricing Reality:

Free: 10 emails/month

Starter: $10/month (unlimited emails)

Premium: $20/month (advanced features)

No hidden costs

Who Should Use MailMaestro: Ideal for individuals or small teams who want simple, effective AI email writing without changing their existing workflow. Great for busy executives who need quick, professional responses.

Deal Breakers: Limited automation features. It’s purely a writing tool, so don’t expect workflow automation or advanced personalization beyond conversation context.

3. Grammarly AI – The Free Powerhouse

The Verdict: 8.1/10

Grammarly’s AI email writer surprised me. It’s completely free, integrates everywhere, and generates genuinely useful email drafts. For occasional users, it’s hard to beat.

What Makes It Special:

Completely free with no usage limits

Works in any text field (Gmail, Outlook, Notion, etc.)

Excellent tone adjustment options

Built-in grammar and style checking

Real Performance:

Setup time: 2 minutes (download app)

Response rate: +8% vs. manual emails

Time saved per week: 3 hours

Learning curve: Instant

Pricing Reality:

Free: Unlimited email generation

Premium: $12/month (advanced features, but not needed for email)

Who Should Use Grammarly: Perfect for individuals who write 10-20 emails per week and want AI assistance without monthly costs. Also great as a backup tool for teams using other primary solutions.

Deal Breakers: No workflow automation or advanced personalization. It’s a writing assistant, not a complete email solution.

4. Superhuman AI – Speed Meets Intelligence

The Verdict: 8.0/10

Superhuman has always been about email speed, and their AI features maintain that focus. The AI writes fast, suggests responses instantly, and integrates perfectly with their productivity-focused email client.

What Makes It Special:

Instant AI suggestions appear as you type

Learns your writing style over time

Integrates with calendar for meeting scheduling

Premium email client with AI built-in

Real Performance:

Setup time: 15 minutes (including email import)

Response rate: +12% vs. manual emails

Time saved per week: 5 hours

Learning curve: Low for existing Superhuman users

Pricing Reality:

$30/month (includes email client + AI features)

No usage limits or hidden costs

Who Should Use Superhuman: Email power users who want a premium email experience with AI baked in. Great for executives and sales teams who live in their inbox.

Deal Breakers: Expensive for AI features alone. You’re paying for the entire Superhuman experience, which might be overkill if you just want AI email writing.

5. Copy.ai – Marketing Email Specialist

The Verdict: 7.8/10

Copy.ai excels at marketing and sales emails. The templates are conversion-focused, and the AI understands sales psychology better than general-purpose tools.

What Makes It Special:

Templates optimized for sales and marketing

A/B testing suggestions built-in

Workflow automation for email sequences

Strong integration with marketing tools

Real Performance:

Setup time: 10 minutes

Response rate: +19% for cold outreach emails

Time saved per week: 4 hours

Learning curve: Low

Pricing Reality:

Free: 2,000 words/month

Pro: $49/month (unlimited)

Hidden costs: Advanced integrations cost extra

Who Should Use Copy.ai: Marketing teams and sales professionals who need conversion-focused email copy. Particularly strong for cold outreach and email marketing campaigns.

Deal Breakers: Less effective for internal communications or customer support emails. It’s built for sales, and that focus shows.

6. Boomerang AI – Scheduling Intelligence

The Verdict: 7.5/10

Boomerang’s AI focuses on timing and follow-up optimization. It not only writes emails but suggests the best time to send them and automatically follows up if needed.

What Makes It Special:

AI-powered send time optimization

Automatic follow-up sequences

Response rate prediction

Built-in email scheduling

Real Performance:

Setup time: 8 minutes

Response rate: +15% (mostly due to timing optimization)

Time saved per week: 4 hours

Learning curve: Low

Pricing Reality:

Basic: $4.98/month

Pro: $14.98/month

Premium: $49.98/month

Who Should Use Boomerang: Sales teams and anyone who needs to track email responses and optimize send times. Great for follow-up heavy workflows.

Deal Breakers: The AI writing quality is good but not exceptional. You’re mainly paying for scheduling and tracking features.

7. Flowrite – Template System Champion

The Verdict: 7.2/10

Flowrite turns bullet points into polished emails. Their template system is comprehensive, and the AI does a solid job expanding brief notes into professional communications.

What Makes It Special:

Excellent template library

Bullet point to full email conversion

Multiple tone options

Browser extension works everywhere

Real Performance:

Setup time: 5 minutes

Response rate: Same as manual emails

Time saved per week: 3 hours

Learning curve: Very low

Pricing Reality:

Light: $4/month (15 emails)

Premium: $12/month (unlimited)

No hidden costs

Who Should Use Flowrite: Perfect for people who know what they want to say but struggle with email formatting and professional tone. Great for non-native English speakers.

Deal Breakers: Limited personalization options and no automation features. It’s strictly a writing assistant.

8. WriteMail.ai – The Chrome Extension Specialist

The Verdict: 6.9/10

WriteMail.ai works as a Chrome extension that integrates with Gmail. It’s simple, affordable, and gets the job done for basic email writing needs.

What Makes It Special:

Simple Chrome extension setup

Works directly in Gmail

Multiple language support

Affordable pricing

Real Performance:

Setup time: 2 minutes

Response rate: -3% vs. manual emails (emails felt slightly robotic)

Time saved per week: 2 hours

Learning curve: None

Pricing Reality:

Basic: $6.25/month

Pro: $17.95/month

Who Should Use WriteMail.ai: Budget-conscious users who need basic AI email writing in Gmail. Good for international teams with multiple language requirements.

Deal Breakers: Limited features and the AI output sometimes sounds obviously generated. Fine for internal emails but risky for external communications.

Tools That Didn’t Make the Cut (And Why)

I tested 6 additional tools that couldn’t compete with the top 8:

Jasper AI: Great for long-form content, terrible for emails. The output was consistently too formal and verbose.

Claude (Direct): Excellent AI, but requires too much manual work. No email-specific features or integrations.

Notion AI: Works only in Notion. Limited email templates and no external integrations.

Rytr: Cheap but generic output. Every email felt like it came from the same robot.

ChatGPT (Direct): Powerful but requires manual prompt engineering. No email workflow features.

Canva Email Writer: Focused on design over content. Better for newsletters than business emails.

Tool	Best For	Price	Setup Time	Response Rate Change	Time Saved/Week
Lindy Winner	End-to-end automation	$39/mo	25 min	+34%	12 hours
MailMaestro	Gmail/Outlook integration	$10/mo	3 min	0%	6 hours
Grammarly AI	Free solution	Free	2 min	+8%	3 hours
Superhuman AI	Premium email experience	$30/mo	15 min	+12%	5 hours
Copy.ai	Marketing emails	$49/mo	10 min	+19%*	4 hours
Boomerang AI	Follow-up automation	$15/mo	8 min	+15%	4 hours
Flowrite	Template-based writing	$12/mo	5 min	0%	3 hours
WriteMail.ai	Budget Gmail solution	$6/mo	2 min	-3%	2 hours

*Copy.ai’s +19% improvement only applies to cold outreach emails. Other email types showed no significant improvement.

How to Choose the Right AI Email Generator for Your Needs

For Solo Entrepreneurs and Freelancers

Go with Grammarly AI if you’re budget-conscious and write fewer than 50 emails per week. It’s free, works everywhere, and provides solid results without the learning curve.

Upgrade to MailMaestro if you need more features and live in Gmail/Outlook. The $10/month is worth it for the time savings and seamless integration.

For Small Businesses (2-10 people)

Start with MailMaestro for the team. It’s affordable, easy to deploy, and doesn’t require workflow changes. Add Lindy later if you need automation.

Consider Superhuman AI if your team already uses premium email tools and values speed above all else.

For Growing Companies (10-50 people)

Lindy is your best bet for scalable email automation. The initial setup investment pays off quickly when you’re handling hundreds of emails per week.

Copy.ai works well for sales and marketing teams who need conversion-focused email copy.

For Enterprise Teams (50+ people)

Lindy or Superhuman AI depending on whether you prioritize automation (Lindy) or email client experience (Superhuman).

Avoid free tools or simple extensions. You need enterprise features, security, and support.

The Hidden Costs Nobody Talks About

After testing these tools for a month, I discovered several hidden costs that vendors don’t advertise:

Integration Fees

Most tools charge extra for CRM integrations beyond basic connections

Advanced automation features often require higher-tier plans

API access typically costs $50-200/month additional

Seat Licensing Surprises

“Per user” pricing kicks in faster than expected

Admin and reporting features often require premium plans

Guest access usually counts as full seats

Usage Limits Reality

“Unlimited” often has fair use policies

Email volume restrictions appear in fine print

Overage charges can double your monthly bill

Training and Onboarding

Complex tools like Lindy require 5-10 hours of initial setup

Team training adds another 2-3 hours per person

Optimization and fine-tuning is ongoing

Pro tip: Always test with real email volume before committing to annual plans. What seems unlimited in demos can hit limits quickly in production.

My Final Recommendation: The 3-Tool Strategy

After a month of real-world testing, here’s the setup I’m actually using:

Primary Tool: Lindy – Handles 80% of my emails through automation Backup Tool: MailMaestro – For quick manual responses when I need more control Free Option: Grammarly AI – Always available in any text field as a safety net

This combination covers every scenario while keeping costs reasonable. The total monthly cost is $49, but I’m saving 15+ hours per week on email tasks.

What’s Coming in 2025: AI Email Trends to Watch

Based on my conversations with tool developers and beta testing several upcoming features:

Voice-to-Email: Record a 30-second voice note, get a polished email. Superhuman and Lindy are both working on this.

Meeting Integration: AI that joins calls, takes notes, and automatically sends follow-ups. Lindy already does this; others are catching up.

Emotional Intelligence: Better understanding of tone and relationship context. Expect more nuanced responses based on email history.

Real-Time Collaboration: AI that helps teams write emails together, similar to Google Docs but for email composition.

Industry-Specific Models: AI trained on specific industries (legal, healthcare, finance) for more accurate professional communication.

FAQ: Best AI Email Generators 2025

Do AI-generated emails hurt response rates?

Based on my testing, well-crafted AI emails perform the same or better than manual emails. The key is choosing tools that understand context and allow customization. Avoid generic templates that sound obviously robotic.

Can clients tell when I use AI to write emails?

In my experience, no. The top tools generate natural-sounding emails that match professional communication styles. However, always review and personalize before sending important messages.

Are AI email generators secure for business use?

Most established tools meet enterprise security standards. Lindy, MailMaestro, and Superhuman all offer SOC 2 compliance and data encryption. Always check privacy policies for data retention practices.

How much time can I realistically save?

In my testing, the average time savings was 5-8 hours per week for someone sending 100+ emails weekly. Your mileage will vary based on email complexity and current writing speed.

What about legal and compliance concerns?

AI-generated emails still require human review for legal, financial, or medical communications. Most tools include disclaimers about professional judgment requirements.

The Bottom Line: Is AI Email Generation Worth It?

After wasting 40 hours testing every tool so you don’t have to, here’s my honest assessment:

Yes, if you’re sending 25+ emails per week. The time savings and consistency improvements justify the monthly cost for most professionals.

Maybe, if you’re sending 10-25 emails per week. Start with Grammarly AI (free) or MailMaestro ($10/month) to test the waters.

No, if you’re sending fewer than 10 emails per week. The learning curve and monthly costs aren’t worth it for light email users.

The tools that truly deliver combine three elements: intelligent writing assistance, workflow integration, and genuine time savings. Lindy, MailMaestro, and Grammarly AI hit all three marks while avoiding the pitfalls that make other tools feel like expensive ChatGPT wrappers.

Remember: the best AI email generator is the one your team will actually use consistently. Start with a free trial, test with real emails, and measure the results. Your inbox (and your sanity) will thank you.

Last updated: June 2025. I update this guide quarterly as new tools launch and existing ones improve. Have a tool suggestion or question about my testing? Send me an email (probably written with AI) at [contact info].

I Wasted 40 Hours Testing AI Email Generators So You Don’t Have To

Best AI email generator 2025 comparison testing results - Best AI email assistant 2025

Best AI Email Generators 2025

Last month, I found myself drowning in emails at 11 PM again. My startup had just onboarded 200 new customers, and I was personally responding to every support ticket, sales inquiry, and partnership request. Something had to change.

That’s when I decided to test every major AI email generator on the market. Not just click around for 10 minutes, but actually use them to handle real business emails for an entire month. I sent 847 emails using 14 different tools, tracked response rates, measured setup time, and even calculated the hidden costs.

The bottom line? Three tools stood out from the pack, but one clear winner emerged that’s saving me 12 hours per week.

Quick Answer: Skip to My Top 3 Picks

If you need an AI email generator right now, here are the only three worth considering:

Lindy – Best overall for businesses ($39/month) – Handles everything from writing to automating follow-ups

MailMaestro – Best for Gmail/Outlook integration ($10/month) – Works seamlessly inside your existing email client

Grammarly AI – Best free option – Perfect for occasional email writing without monthly fees

Keep reading to see my detailed testing results, hidden pricing gotchas, and which tools actually hurt my response rates.

What Makes an AI Email Generator Actually Useful in 2025?

After burning through a month of real emails, I learned that most “AI email generators” are just ChatGPT wrappers with fancy interfaces. The tools that actually move the needle have three key features:

Context Awareness: Can it understand your conversation history, not just generate generic text?

Workflow Integration: Does it fit into how you actually work, or force you to copy-paste between 12 different tabs?

Real Personalization: Beyond swapping in {first_name}, can it pull relevant details from your CRM, previous emails, or company data?

My Testing Method: Real Emails, Real Results

I didn’t just play around with demo accounts. Here’s exactly how I tested each tool:

847 real emails sent across sales outreach, customer support, partnership inquiries, and internal communications

Response rate tracking for each tool to see which generated emails people actually responded to

Setup time measurement from account creation to sending the first useful email

Hidden cost analysis including integrations, seat licenses, and usage limits

Team feedback from my three co-founders who also tested the tools

Every tool was evaluated on the same criteria: Does it actually save time without making me sound like a robot?

The 8 AI Email Generators That Made My Final List

1. Lindy – The Email Automation Powerhouse

The Verdict: 9.2/10

Lindy isn’t just an email writer, it’s like having a personal assistant who never sleeps. After setting up my “Email Agent,” it was automatically triaging my inbox, drafting responses, and even scheduling follow-ups based on context.

What Makes It Special:

Creates custom AI agents that understand your business context

Automatically joins Zoom calls, takes notes, and sends follow-ups

Integrates with 3,000+ tools including HubSpot, Slack, and Gmail

Can handle entire email workflows, not just writing

Real Performance:

Setup time: 25 minutes (including CRM integration)

Response rate improvement: +34% vs. my manual emails

Time saved per week: 12 hours

Learning curve: Moderate – took 3 days to optimize prompts

Pricing Reality:

Starter: $39/month (300 tasks)

Professional: $99/month (3,000 tasks)

Hidden costs: None if you stay within task limits

Who Should Use Lindy: Perfect for growing businesses that need end-to-end email automation. If you’re sending 50+ emails per week and want AI to handle the entire process from drafting to follow-up scheduling, this is your tool.

Deal Breakers: The learning curve is real. Expect to spend a week fine-tuning your agents. Also, the task-based pricing can get expensive if you’re not strategic about automation setup.

2. MailMaestro – Gmail Integration Done Right

The Verdict: 8.9/10

MailMaestro wins on pure convenience. It works directly inside Gmail and Outlook with a simple browser extension. No copy-pasting, no switching tabs, no disruption to your existing workflow.

What Makes It Special:

Lives inside your email client with one-click access

Understands conversation context automatically

Offers 3 different email drafts to choose from

Smart template system for repetitive emails

Real Performance:

Setup time: 3 minutes (just install the extension)

Response rate: Same as manual emails (no improvement, but no decrease)

Time saved per week: 6 hours

Learning curve: Zero – works immediately

Pricing Reality:

Free: 10 emails/month

Starter: $10/month (unlimited emails)

Premium: $20/month (advanced features)

No hidden costs

Who Should Use MailMaestro: Ideal for individuals or small teams who want simple, effective AI email writing without changing their existing workflow. Great for busy executives who need quick, professional responses.

Deal Breakers: Limited automation features. It’s purely a writing tool, so don’t expect workflow automation or advanced personalization beyond conversation context.

3. Grammarly AI – The Free Powerhouse

The Verdict: 8.1/10

Grammarly’s AI email writer surprised me. It’s completely free, integrates everywhere, and generates genuinely useful email drafts. For occasional users, it’s hard to beat.

&lt;iframe id="google_ads_frame1"&gt;

What Makes It Special:

Completely free with no usage limits

Works in any text field (Gmail, Outlook, Notion, etc.)

Excellent tone adjustment options

Built-in grammar and style checking

Real Performance:

Setup time: 2 minutes (download app)

Response rate: +8% vs. manual emails

Time saved per week: 3 hours

Learning curve: Instant

Pricing Reality:

Free: Unlimited email generation

Premium: $12/month (advanced features, but not needed for email)

Who Should Use Grammarly: Perfect for individuals who write 10-20 emails per week and want AI assistance without monthly costs. Also great as a backup tool for teams using other primary solutions.

Deal Breakers: No workflow automation or advanced personalization. It’s a writing assistant, not a complete email solution.

4. Superhuman AI – Speed Meets Intelligence

The Verdict: 8.0/10

Superhuman has always been about email speed, and their AI features maintain that focus. The AI writes fast, suggests responses instantly, and integrates perfectly with their productivity-focused email client.

What Makes It Special:

Instant AI suggestions appear as you type

Learns your writing style over time

Integrates with calendar for meeting scheduling

Premium email client with AI built-in

Real Performance:

Setup time: 15 minutes (including email import)

Response rate: +12% vs. manual emails

Time saved per week: 5 hours

Learning curve: Low for existing Superhuman users

Pricing Reality:

$30/month (includes email client + AI features)

No usage limits or hidden costs

Who Should Use Superhuman: Email power users who want a premium email experience with AI baked in. Great for executives and sales teams who live in their inbox.

Deal Breakers: Expensive for AI features alone. You’re paying for the entire Superhuman experience, which might be overkill if you just want AI email writing.

5. Copy.ai – Marketing Email Specialist

The Verdict: 7.8/10

Copy.ai excels at marketing and sales emails. The templates are conversion-focused, and the AI understands sales psychology better than general-purpose tools.

What Makes It Special:

Templates optimized for sales and marketing

A/B testing suggestions built-in

Workflow automation for email sequences

Strong integration with marketing tools

Real Performance:

Setup time: 10 minutes

Response rate: +19% for cold outreach emails

Time saved per week: 4 hours

Learning curve: Low

Pricing Reality:

Free: 2,000 words/month

Pro: $49/month (unlimited)

Hidden costs: Advanced integrations cost extra

Who Should Use Copy.ai: Marketing teams and sales professionals who need conversion-focused email copy. Particularly strong for cold outreach and email marketing campaigns.

Deal Breakers: Less effective for internal communications or customer support emails. It’s built for sales, and that focus shows.

6. Boomerang AI – Scheduling Intelligence

The Verdict: 7.5/10

Boomerang’s AI focuses on timing and follow-up optimization. It not only writes emails but suggests the best time to send them and automatically follows up if needed.

What Makes It Special:

AI-powered send time optimization

Automatic follow-up sequences

Response rate prediction

Built-in email scheduling

Real Performance:

Setup time: 8 minutes

Response rate: +15% (mostly due to timing optimization)

Time saved per week: 4 hours

Learning curve: Low

Pricing Reality:

Basic: $4.98/month

Pro: $14.98/month

Premium: $49.98/month

Who Should Use Boomerang: Sales teams and anyone who needs to track email responses and optimize send times. Great for follow-up heavy workflows.

Deal Breakers: The AI writing quality is good but not exceptional. You’re mainly paying for scheduling and tracking features.

7. Flowrite – Template System Champion

The Verdict: 7.2/10

Flowrite turns bullet points into polished emails. Their template system is comprehensive, and the AI does a solid job expanding brief notes into professional communications.

What Makes It Special:

Excellent template library

Bullet point to full email conversion

Multiple tone options

Browser extension works everywhere

Real Performance:

Setup time: 5 minutes

Response rate: Same as manual emails

Time saved per week: 3 hours

Learning curve: Very low

Pricing Reality:

Light: $4/month (15 emails)

Premium: $12/month (unlimited)

No hidden costs

Who Should Use Flowrite: Perfect for people who know what they want to say but struggle with email formatting and professional tone. Great for non-native English speakers.

Deal Breakers: Limited personalization options and no automation features. It’s strictly a writing assistant.

8. WriteMail.ai – The Chrome Extension Specialist

The Verdict: 6.9/10

WriteMail.ai works as a Chrome extension that integrates with Gmail. It’s simple, affordable, and gets the job done for basic email writing needs.

What Makes It Special:

Simple Chrome extension setup

Works directly in Gmail

Multiple language support

Affordable pricing

Real Performance:

Setup time: 2 minutes

Response rate: -3% vs. manual emails (emails felt slightly robotic)

Time saved per week: 2 hours

Learning curve: None

Pricing Reality:

Basic: $6.25/month

Pro: $17.95/month

Who Should Use WriteMail.ai: Budget-conscious users who need basic AI email writing in Gmail. Good for international teams with multiple language requirements.

Deal Breakers: Limited features and the AI output sometimes sounds obviously generated. Fine for internal emails but risky for external communications.

Tools That Didn’t Make the Cut (And Why)

I tested 6 additional tools that couldn’t compete with the top 8:

Jasper AI: Great for long-form content, terrible for emails. The output was consistently too formal and verbose.

Claude (Direct): Excellent AI, but requires too much manual work. No email-specific features or integrations.

Notion AI: Works only in Notion. Limited email templates and no external integrations.

Rytr: Cheap but generic output. Every email felt like it came from the same robot.

ChatGPT (Direct): Powerful but requires manual prompt engineering. No email workflow features.

Canva Email Writer: Focused on design over content. Better for newsletters than business emails.

AI Email Generator Comparison: The Real Data

Based on 40 hours of testing with 847 real emails sent

Tool	Best For	Price	Setup Time	Response Rate Change	Time Saved/Week
Lindy Winner	End-to-end automation	$39/mo	25 min	+34%	12 hours
MailMaestro	Gmail/Outlook integration	$10/mo	3 min	0%	6 hours
Grammarly AI	Free solution	Free	2 min	+8%	3 hours
Superhuman AI	Premium email experience	$30/mo	15 min	+12%	5 hours
Copy.ai	Marketing emails	$49/mo	10 min	+19%*	4 hours
Boomerang AI	Follow-up automation	$15/mo	8 min	+15%	4 hours
Flowrite	Template-based writing	$12/mo	5 min	0%	3 hours
WriteMail.ai	Budget Gmail solution	$6/mo	2 min	-3%	2 hours

*Copy.ai’s +19% improvement only applies to cold outreach emails. Other email types showed no significant improvement.

How to Choose the Right AI Email Generator for Your Needs

For Solo Entrepreneurs and Freelancers

Go with Grammarly AI if you’re budget-conscious and write fewer than 50 emails per week. It’s free, works everywhere, and provides solid results without the learning curve.

Upgrade to MailMaestro if you need more features and live in Gmail/Outlook. The $10/month is worth it for the time savings and seamless integration.

For Small Businesses (2-10 people)

Start with MailMaestro for the team. It’s affordable, easy to deploy, and doesn’t require workflow changes. Add Lindy later if you need automation.

Consider Superhuman AI if your team already uses premium email tools and values speed above all else.

For Growing Companies (10-50 people)

Lindy is your best bet for scalable email automation. The initial setup investment pays off quickly when you’re handling hundreds of emails per week.

Copy.ai works well for sales and marketing teams who need conversion-focused email copy.

For Enterprise Teams (50+ people)

Lindy or Superhuman AI depending on whether you prioritize automation (Lindy) or email client experience (Superhuman).

Avoid free tools or simple extensions. You need enterprise features, security, and support.

The Hidden Costs Nobody Talks About

After testing these tools for a month, I discovered several hidden costs that vendors don’t advertise:

Integration Fees

Most tools charge extra for CRM integrations beyond basic connections

Advanced automation features often require higher-tier plans

API access typically costs $50-200/month additional

Seat Licensing Surprises

“Per user” pricing kicks in faster than expected

Admin and reporting features often require premium plans

Guest access usually counts as full seats

Usage Limits Reality

“Unlimited” often has fair use policies

Email volume restrictions appear in fine print

Overage charges can double your monthly bill

Training and Onboarding

Complex tools like Lindy require 5-10 hours of initial setup

Team training adds another 2-3 hours per person

Optimization and fine-tuning is ongoing

Pro tip: Always test with real email volume before committing to annual plans. What seems unlimited in demos can hit limits quickly in production.

My Final Recommendation: The 3-Tool Strategy

After a month of real-world testing, here’s the setup I’m actually using:

Primary Tool: Lindy – Handles 80% of my emails through automation Backup Tool: MailMaestro – For quick manual responses when I need more control Free Option: Grammarly AI – Always available in any text field as a safety net

This combination covers every scenario while keeping costs reasonable. The total monthly cost is $49, but I’m saving 15+ hours per week on email tasks.

What’s Coming in 2025: AI Email Trends to Watch

Based on my conversations with tool developers and beta testing several upcoming features:

Voice-to-Email: Record a 30-second voice note, get a polished email. Superhuman and Lindy are both working on this.

Meeting Integration: AI that joins calls, takes notes, and automatically sends follow-ups. Lindy already does this; others are catching up.

Emotional Intelligence: Better understanding of tone and relationship context. Expect more nuanced responses based on email history.

Real-Time Collaboration: AI that helps teams write emails together, similar to Google Docs but for email composition.

Industry-Specific Models: AI trained on specific industries (legal, healthcare, finance) for more accurate professional communication.

&lt;iframe id="google_ads_frame3"&gt;

FAQ: Best AI Email Generators 2025

Do AI-generated emails hurt response rates?

Based on my testing, well-crafted AI emails perform the same or better than manual emails. The key is choosing tools that understand context and allow customization. Avoid generic templates that sound obviously robotic.

Can clients tell when I use AI to write emails?

In my experience, no. The top tools generate natural-sounding emails that match professional communication styles. However, always review and personalize before sending important messages.

Are AI email generators secure for business use?

Most established tools meet enterprise security standards. Lindy, MailMaestro, and Superhuman all offer SOC 2 compliance and data encryption. Always check privacy policies for data retention practices.

How much time can I realistically save?

In my testing, the average time savings was 5-8 hours per week for someone sending 100+ emails weekly. Your mileage will vary based on email complexity and current writing speed.

What about legal and compliance concerns?

AI-generated emails still require human review for legal, financial, or medical communications. Most tools include disclaimers about professional judgment requirements.

The Bottom Line: Is AI Email Generation Worth It?

After wasting 40 hours testing every tool so you don’t have to, here’s my honest assessment:

Yes, if you’re sending 25+ emails per week. The time savings and consistency improvements justify the monthly cost for most professionals.

Maybe, if you’re sending 10-25 emails per week. Start with Grammarly AI (free) or MailMaestro ($10/month) to test the waters.

No, if you’re sending fewer than 10 emails per week. The learning curve and monthly costs aren’t worth it for light email users.

The tools that truly deliver combine three elements: intelligent writing assistance, workflow integration, and genuine time savings. Lindy, MailMaestro, and Grammarly AI hit all three marks while avoiding the pitfalls that make other tools feel like expensive ChatGPT wrappers.

Remember: the best AI email generator is the one your team will actually use consistently. Start with a free trial, test with real emails, and measure the results. Your inbox (and your sanity) will thank you.

If you want to enjoy the most thrilling way to bet on sports, we recommend that you try live betting. You can wager on sports such as football and tennis as they unfold in real-time at MarathonBet Italy, with plenty of markets available for single, multi and system bets.

Multiples Bets

MarathonBet provides users with a chance to make alternative bets to single bets. Multiple bets allow you to add several markets to one bet. When you click on the Multi tab within the bet slip, the odds of all the markets will be calculated together for you to place one stake on.

You can add up to 20 markets to your multi bet. However, to be successful, all of your selections must come through. This is why your odds to win will reduce with every new selection. We therefore recommend that you be more conservative with your picks for a multi, or make low-stake bets.

Another supported alternative to multis is the system bets. System bets are similar to multis in that you can make multiple market selections though you can still earn a payout if some legs don’t come through. You will find the available systems as you make your picks.

Bet and Win Limits at MarathonBet Italy

Like all major betting sites MarathonBet sets limits on how much you can win with a single bet. In any case, you are able to wager from as little as 1c. This is very accommodating to low-budget players. As for maximum bets, this will depend on whether the potential win will exceed the payout cap.

Many of these sports are stocked with a large selection of tournaments, events and leagues. There are even categories for major events such as the Olympics or the Super Bowl.

Some of the featured well-stocked and popular MarathonBet sports include football, tennis, basketball, ice hockey, the Big Four US major sports leagues, golf and motorsports such as Formula 1. Below, we’ve listed some of the most popular sports and leagues to bet on at MarathonBet.

The English Premier League, Italian Serie A and the FIFA World Cup generate huge bettor attention, and players are able to make many different bet types such as money lines, over/unders, player props, futures and much more

Bettors can also bet on niche markets such as politics, reality TV show outcomes and awards shows. There are also several eSports markets available, including for League of Legends and DOTA 2. For this reason, all bettors should be satisfied with their options at this bookie.

In-play Betting & Live Streaming

If you want to enjoy the most thrilling way to bet on sports, we recommend that you try live betting. You can wager on sports such as football and tennis as they unfold in real-time at MarathonBet Italy, with plenty of markets available for single, multi and system bets.

To get started, head to the Live tab where you will find an overview of the events that are currently in play. You can either make selections from this pge, or click on the events to find more markets for each game. You will also be able to view accurate statistics to help you make the most accurate bets as possible.

One of the biggest advantages of MarathonBet is that there is live streaming available. This is a feature that allows you to watch games as you wager on them. Streams will usually include bet suggestions and graphic overlays so that you can quickly react to take advantage of the best prices.

Multiples Bets

MarathonBet provides users with a chance to make alternative bets to single bets. Multiple bets allow you to add several markets to one bet. When you click on the Multi tab within the bet slip, the odds of all the markets will be calculated together for you to place one stake on.

You can add up to 20 markets to your multi bet. However, to be successful, all of your selections must come through. This is why your odds to win will reduce with every new selection. We therefore recommend that you be more conservative with your picks for a multi, or make low-stake bets.

Another supported alternative to multis is the system bets. System bets are similar to multis in that you can make multiple market selections though you can still earn a payout if some legs don’t come through. You will find the available systems as you make your picks.

Bet and Win Limits at MarathonBet Italy

Like all major betting sites MarathonBet sets limits on how much you can win with a single bet. In any case, you are able to wager from as little as 1c. This is very accommodating to low-budget players. As for maximum bets, this will depend on whether the potential win will exceed the payout cap.

Single bet payouts are capped at €10,000 per bet. This is in accordance with Italian online gambling regulations and is the case at all bookmaker sites. For multiples and systems, winnings are capped at €10,000 per line and €50,000 in total for all winning lines. There are no daily win limits.

Competitive Odds Throughout

The average MarathonBet house edge is 4.5%, which is very reasonable. The house edge informs the odds at betting sites, and the lower it is, the higher that odds can be. Keep in mind that that is just the average for all sports, and some sports will actually have much smaller payout percentages.

The major sports tend to offer better payouts so that they can be more competitive, hence why football odds are usually so fair. This means that less popular markets will suffer to make up for any loss in profits. You can find the average payout variances according to MarathonBet sports below.

The High-Power Platform

As soon as you open MarathonBet, you’ll notice that it has a clean and simple design that makes it easy to find exactly what you’re looking for. The site uses a blue and grey colour scheme that gives the site a professional atmosphere. The technical aspects are just as considered as the aesthetics.

The pre-match lobby lists sports based on popularity and when each category is clicked, you can view all available leagues. It makes navigating through the tabs and building bets easy.

The pages quickly load and the site rarely crashes due to its stripped back design and there is a seamless cashier system to facilitate prompt payments. There are plenty of useful guides and FAQs listed so that new players will be able to get used to the site with easy. Overall, MarathonBet offers a great user experience.

How to Place a Bet

The first thing you need to do before you can place a bet with MarathonBet is create an account. This is a straight-forward process that will be complete as soon as you have verified your identity. After this is complete, you will be able to make your deposits and claim the welcome bonus.

To build your bet, head to the MarathonBet sports lobby. Search for your favourite sports and find the markets that interest you. Click on the odds to add them to your bet slip and decide whether you want to make a single, system or multi bet. We’ve created and shared a three-step betting guide below.

Open an account

Click Join, then provide your identification documents so that you can be verified. Once this is complete, make a deposit and claim the welcome bonus.

[2] Find a sports market

Find a sports market

[3] Enter your wager

Enter your wager

Company Info

It is also important for us to pass on what we know about MarathonBet’s parent company so you can make a fully informed decision as to whether you want to wager with this casino or not. Take a read through the sections below for information on MarathonBet’s parent company and its history.

MarathonBet was launched in 1997 as retail bookmaker and within years was one of the first sites to offer online sports betting. The MarathonBet Italy site now caters to millions of users around Europe. In te upcoming sections, you will learn more about the business, its licensing details and customer support options.

The Business Under the Microscope

MarathonBet is operated by an independent company that was launched in 1997 in the CiS. In 2002, the company branched into the online gambling market. The site holds licences in several other European nations such as Spain, Belarus and the UK and is registered in the Dutch Caribbean Island of Curaçao.

The company has developed a loyal following across many countries that it operates in. One of the biggest indicators of its commitment to working closely with sports teams is its numerous sponsorships of major teams. Currently, it is a sponsor of Manchester City FC, one of the UK’s top Premier League teams.

Customer Support

It’s a reality that issues can arise at any time when using online betting sites, just as they can with any website. Considering the financial nature of betting, it’s essential that all bookmakers offer fast and accessible service avenues. The quality of a bookie’s customer care is an important quality of our reviews.

We were glad to find in our review that customer support is available through live chat and email. Live chat is the most convenient support method and tends to have the shortest wait times. However, the lack of 24/7 support is disappointing, as service hours are between 10AM and 6 PM daily.

Support is available in Italian and English, so our readers are sure to be satisfied with this. We tested the customer care experience and found that the agents were very helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. For this reason, we have given high marks for this section of our MarathonBet review.

Licensing & Security

MarathonBet is licensed in Italy which is important, as it’s against the law for Italians to gamble with unlicensed sites. It is also extremely unsafe, as licensing ensures that sites are secure, fair and safe. It also guarantees that you will always have legal protection in case a site doesn’t pay out your owed winnings.

The bookie is also licensed in Spain, Belarus, the UK and Curacao. To maintain its safety, MarathonBet has integrated 256-bit SSL encryption technology. This keeps players’ sensitive information safeguarded from hackers. It has also been independently fairness tested and proven to offer fair gambling products.

The MarathonBet sportsbook collaborates with responsible gambling organisations to protect at-risk players from gambling harms. These organisations include GambleAware, GamCare and Gamblers Anonymous. The use of the KYC identity verification system prevents minors and self-excluded players from joining.

Bonus Points

# Page 3
3 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  Dear Reader,  I am proud to present our 2023 edition of iComply’s annual Regwatch Report, a comprehensive look  at the global landscape of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regulations and compliance. Now in its 4th  edition, these reports have served as a valuable resource for government officials, board members, compliance officers, executives, and lawyers involved in global AML compliance. As we look to the future, we expect to see continued evolution of AML regulations and increased focus on emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and blockchain. We also expect increased international cooperation among regulatory authorities, as well as more stringent regulations for virtual assets and even greater emphasis on beneficial ownership transparency. At iComply, we are committed to helping organizations navigate the ever-changing landscape of financial regulations and compliance. We hope that this report will serve as a valuable tool in your efforts to effectively serve your customers and protect your organization from financial crime. It is our goal that by reading this report, you will better understand the current state of AML regulations and compliance and gain a clearer sense of what to expect in the future. We encourage you to share this report with your colleagues, peers, clients, or board members within your organization and network. Thank you for reading,  Matthew Unger  Chief Executive Officer  Letter from our CEO
# Page 4
4  THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  About iComply  iComply Investor Services is a technology company  that builds compliance infrastructure for the digital  economy. We strive to create a secure, transparent, and equitable global financial system, where compliance  is embedded seamlessly into every transaction.  Our products enable businesses of all sizes to bring  compliance into their applications and operational processes.  At iComply, we believe that financial literacy, accessibility, and accountability should be at the  heart of every transaction. Our mission is to make  the financial transaction process more secure and trustworthy, helping to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing. We strive to create a world where digital transactions are both efficient and sustainable.
# Page 5
5 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  Global Overview:  AML Regulations and Trends  Today’s global AML landscape is changing rapidly as new technologies, criminal tactics, and regulatory developments continually emerge. In response to these developments, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF),  the major international body responsible for setting  global standards for AML and combating the financing of terrorism (CFT), has outlined its priorities. Over the next two years, these priorities include strengthening asset recovery, tackling illicit finance associated with cyber-enabled crime, increasing the effectiveness of global AML measures, and reinforcing  partnerships with FATF-style regional bodies. With regulatory scrutiny and enforcement increasing  in the digital economy, there is a growing demand for emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, and biometric technologies to be used in  AML compliance.  However, the implementation of these regulations and  technologies comes with their own set of challenges  and potential drawbacks. In order to ensure a safe and secure financial system, it is important to stay abreast  of the latest developments and adapt accordingly.  As new technological and financial innovations  bring both opportunities and challenges for money  launderers and regulators alike, leaders in government, finance, and technology must cooperate to ensure transparency in beneficial ownership. To effectively address these issues, both regulatory bodies and financial institutions have begun to  collaborate and share information and best practices. Regulatory bodies in a number of countries have  issued new regulations and licensing requirements for virtual asset exchanges and service providers, as well as enacted new or updated laws and regulations to improve transparency in ultimate beneficial ownership. the growing utilization of   virtual assets and cryptocurrencies , which are used to anonymously  send funds and bypass conventional AML controls; the increasing use of   advanced technologies   such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, and biometrics by criminals to launder money efficiently; and the growing utilization of   shell companies   and other legal entities to conceal the true owners of assets and disguise the proceeds of crime; and  the COVID-19 pandemic drastically increased use of   digital platforms and online transactions , having a massive impact on AML monitoring and compliance effectiveness.  In 2022, four major issues arose:
# Page 6
Highlights from AML regulators around the world  United States  The United States has an ever-adapting approach to AML regulations and has taken steps to close loopholes  typically exploited by criminals and illicit actors. The US Treasury released the 2022 National Illicit Finance Strategy, which was published to address threats and vulnerabilities identified in its National Risk  Assessment. These threats have been heightened by  fraud, corruption, and the digitization of finance, with  particular emphasis on Russian aggression in Ukraine and the global network of corrupt Russian elites.  To combat this, the U.S. has increased transparency in ultimate beneficial ownership by making it more difficult for criminals to hide behind shell companies and other opaque legal entities. As a result, this will  allow the U.S. to identify and prosecute those who are attempting to skirt around AML regulations. Both the US Treasury and the Financial Crimes  Enforcement Network (FinCEN) have emphasized  the urgent need for strong crypto regulations to  combat global and domestic criminal activities. In particular, FinCEN has proposed a new cryptocurrency  regulation to impose data collection requirements on  crypto exchanges and wallets. While FinCEN does not consider cryptocurrencies legal tender, it does consider cryptocurrency exchanges to be money transmitters,  with tokens viewed as “other value that substitutes for currency.”  Debate in Congress has continued into 2023 over which of the nation’s top regulators, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) or the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), should take the lead on crypto oversight. Separately, the SEC has made it clear it considers most digital assets securities, a designation that brings with it an extensive set of requirements;  while the top U.S. banking regulators issued a sweeping statement on the dangers of crypto. While debate  continues, we expect to see a new set of rules regarding  cryptocurrency and digital assets released in late 2023.  THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  6
# Page 7
7 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  Discussion of the challenges and trends in the U.S. AML landscape  The Cryptocurrency Industry  Despite not being recognized as legal tender, FinCEN has  proposed a new rule that would require cryptocurrency  exchanges and wallets to  report suspicious activity of transactions worth more  than USD 10,000, and to  identify wallet owners when  sending more than $3,000  in a single transaction.  This rule is expected to be  implemented by Fall 2023.  01.  The United States has a complex framework for AML compliance, with various regulatory bodies overseeing different aspects. The fragmented nature of this landscape can create confusion and inconsistencies in standards and reporting requirements, especially in the absence of a centralized authority. To address this, three key areas of focus have been identified.  The Use of Third-party Technology  This area is gaining traction  to combat financial crime.  Financial institutions are increasingly relying on screening and monitoring  solutions, and are utilizing  advanced analytics to detect suspicious patterns and identify high-risk customers.  Through these measures,  the U.S. hopes to improve its AML compliance framework.  Increased Transparency in  Beneficial Ownership  The Corporate Transparency  Act, enacted in January 2021,  requires certain companies  to disclose their beneficial  owners to FinCEN. This policy  is expected to make it more difficult for criminals to hide  behind shell companies and other legal entities.  02.   03.
# Page 8
8 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  Government agencies, priorities, and initiatives  As a whole, the United States government is prioritizing the strengthening of laws and regulations to tackle illicit financial flows, modernizing and building regulatory and enforcement frameworks—particularly in the crypto space—and targeting wrongdoers who seek access to the U.S. financial system in order to launder  the proceeds of crime.  The main agencies involved in AML regulation and enforcement include:  These agencies are working closely with each other and with international partners to combat money  laundering and financial crimes, with a particular focus on cybercrime and virtual currency-related threats.  Financial Crimes Enforcement  Network (FinCEN):  This is the primary agency responsible for enforcing AML regulations in the  U.S. It is a bureau of the Department  of the Treasury and is responsible for  issuing guidance, regulations, and  enforcing compliance with AML laws and  regulations. FinCEN’s current priorities include combating illicit finance related to cybercrime, promoting transparency in beneficial ownership, and increasing AML  measures in the cryptocurrency space.  Securities and Exchange Commission  (SEC):  The SEC is responsible for enforcing AML  regulations in the securities industry, including virtual currency exchanges and initial coin offerings (ICOs). The agency  recently proposed new rules to require  crypto exchanges to register with the SEC  and comply with AML regulations.  Commodity Futures Trading  Commission (CFTC):  The CFTC is responsible for enforcing  AML regulations in the derivatives market,  including virtual currencies. The agency has issued guidance on AML compliance  for virtual currency businesses, and is  working to increase its oversight of the crypto derivatives market.  Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI):  The FBI is responsible for investigating financial crimes, including money  laundering and fraud. The agency has several task forces dedicated to  combating money laundering, and is  increasingly focused on cybercrime and  virtual currency-related financial crimes.  Department of Justice (DOJ):  The DOJ is responsible for prosecuting financial crimes, including money  laundering. The agency has a number of initiatives in place to combat money  laundering, including the creation of  a new task force to focus on virtual  currency-related financial crimes.  Internal Revenue Service (IRS):  The IRS is responsible for enforcing AML regulations related to taxes, including the reporting of suspicious financial  transactions. The agency has issued  guidance on the tax treatment of virtual  currencies and is focused on identifying and prosecuting individuals and businesses that use virtual currencies to  evade taxes.

10 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  The United States has seen a significant amount of enforcement activity in the past year, with various regulatory agencies imposing hefty fines for AML violations. The largest fines were issued by FinCEN, with Bittrex, Inc. paying USD $24 million and BMO Harris Bank paying $60 million for AML violations. JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo were also fined for AML failures, with fines of $250 million and $1 billion respectively. In March 2022, FinCEN issued an alert addressing  increased money laundering concerns in light of the  ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine, particularly for known politically-exposed persons (PEPs) and those with ties to unsanctioned financial activities in support  of Russia. FinCEN also continues to develop regulations  to implement the beneficial ownership registry created  through the Corporate Transparency Act (CTA) and  is seeking assistance to modernize the Bank Secrecy  Act (BSA) as required by the Anti-Money Landering Act (AMLA) of 2020. These enforcement actions highlight the increasing importance of proper AML controls and the severe consequences of not complying with regulations. # Page 11
THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT Canada  The current state of AML regulations in Canada is relatively advanced, with the country being one of the first to regulate virtual currencies under its existing anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing laws. The federal government and provincial securities regulators have jurisdiction over AML regulations, which are enforced by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). FINTRAC serves as the primary Canadian regulatory body for AML compliance, working closely with other government agencies such as the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) to detect and prevent money laundering and terrorist financing activities.  Discussion of the challenges and trends in the Canadian AML landscape  Canada has adopted a proactive approach in dealing  with cryptocurrencies, bringing entities dealing in virtual currencies under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) as  early as 2014. The Canadian government also plans to  strengthen AML regulations with a focus on beneficial  ownership transparency.  Despite these proactive initiatives, there are ongoing  challenges in the Canadian AML landscape such as  difficulties in tracking cross-border transactions, the emergence of new technologies utilized in money laundering activities, and concerns regarding the lack of  coordination between federal and provincial regulators in enforcing AML regulations.  The CRA has also identified the use of virtual currency in tax evasion and has implemented measures to address this issue. FINTRAC has emphasized the need  for increased reporting and monitoring of virtual currency transactions to combat money laundering and  terrorist financing.  Government agencies, priorities, and initiatives  The Canadian government is facing mounting pressure to address the use of cryptocurrencies in money laundering and other illicit activities such as human  and drug trafficking, as well as the escalating threat of cybercrime. The globalization of financial markets and the increasing reliance on technology in financial  transactions have made it increasingly challenging to detect and prevent money laundering activities.  To address these challenges, Canada has implemented  various policies such as the National Risk Assessment  of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, which assesses the money laundering and terrorist financing risks in Canada, and the Action Plan to Combat Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, which outlines the government’s strategy to address these risks. On April 5, 2022, changes proposed to the Proceeds  of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing  Act (PCMLTFA) came into effect. These changes were  initially implemented as an emergency response to the protest convoys occupying major Canadian urban  areas but are now permanently in force, modifying important aspects of the PCMLTFA’s main regulation,  SOR/2002-184. These changes are likely to have  significant implications for service providers offering crowdfunding, payment processing, mortgage brokers, and lending companies, which are now subject to AML  regulations.  11

THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT 13  Singapore  The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) serves as the regulatory body responsible for supervising Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) measures in the city-state.  Singapore’s tax authority, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS), classifies Bitcoin as “goods” and applies Goods & Services Tax accordingly.  Singapore has implemented the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards for AML/CFT and has established a robust framework for AML/CFT measures  in the financial sector. The MAS has also begun to focus  on emerging risks associated with virtual assets and has implemented regulations for virtual asset service providers as a means of mitigating these risks.  While cryptocurrency exchanges and trading are legal in Singapore, the city-state has taken a friendlier  position on the issue than some of its regional  neighbors, as Singapore has worked to establish itself as a hub for traditional financial markets. These latest  developments have helped to establish support for cryptocurrency market activity while implementing stricter AML regulations.  Discussion of the challenges and trends in the Singaporean AML landscape  Singapore has adopted a risk-based approach for Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing  of Terrorism (AML/CFT) regulations, with a focus on  customer due diligence and transaction monitoring. These regulations align with the international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).  Key trends in Singapore’s AML landscape include:  I.   The increasing use of technology in AML compliance.   The Monetary Authority of Singapore  (MAS) has been promoting the use of artificial  intelligence and machine learning to enhance  financial institutions’ AML capabilities. The central bank is also exploring the use of blockchain  technology for AML compliance.  II.   Virtual assets and cryptocurrency.   The MAS has introduced a licensing regime for virtual asset  service providers (VASPs) to ensure AML/CFT compliance in this sector. The VASP Act, which came into effect in October 2020, empowers the MAS to supervise VASPs and implement the FATF’s  guidance on a risk-based approach for this sector.  Despite these efforts, Singapore is considered a high-  risk country for money laundering due to its open  economy, free port status, and large foreign workforce. The country’s real estate sector is also identified as a  potential money laundering risk. The government has  taken steps to address these risks, such as introducing  stricter regulations for real estate agents and tightening laws on shell companies.  Overall, Singapore’s AML landscape is constantly evolving, with both the government and financial  institutions working together to address new risks and  challenges. Increased focus on technology and virtual assets, as well as the commitment to international standards, positions Singapore well to combat money  laundering in the digital age.

15 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  19   https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2022/ubs-ag-singapore-branch-fined-for-anti-money-laundering-violations  20   https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2022/united-overseas-bank-singapore-fined-for-anti-money-laundering-violations  21   https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2022/dbs-bank-singapore-fined-for-anti-money-laundering-violations  22   https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2022/maybank-singapore-fined-for-anti-money-laundering-violations  23   https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2022/standard-chartered-bank-singapore-fined-for-anti-money-laundering-violations  Standard Chartered Bank  Singapore   was   fined SGD  1.7 million by the Monetary Authority of Singapore   (MAS) for AML failures. T he bank  failed to conduct sufficient  customer due diligence on its high-risk clients and had inadequate systems in place for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions.   The  MAS identified that the bank  did not have proper controls in place to identify and assess the money laundering and terrorism  financing risks associated with  its correspondent banking  activities. Additionally, the  bank had inadequate customer due diligence measures in  place, particularly in relation  to its high-risk clients and transactions.   21  DBS Bank   was   fined SGD  2.4 million by the Monetary Authority of Singapore   (MAS) for AML failures.   The bank had inadequate systems in place for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions.   The  MAS identified that the bank  had inadequate transaction monitoring systems in place to  detect suspicious transactions,  particularly those related to its correspondent banking activities.   22  UBS AG Singapore Branch  was   fined SGD 1.3 million  by the Monetary Authority of Singapore   (MAS) for AML  failures,   inadequate systems in place for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions, inadequate transaction monitoring systems in place to detect suspicious transactions,  particularly those related to its correspondent banking  activities, and inadequate  customer due diligence  measures in place, particularly  in relation to its high-risk clients and transactions.   23
# Page 16
16 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  United Overseas Bank (UOB)  Singapore was   fined SGD 1.3  million by the Monetary  Authority of Singapore (MAS)  for AML failures,   inadequate systems for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions,   inadequate transaction monitoring systems in place to detect suspicious  transactions, and inadequate  customer due diligence  measures in place, particularly  in relation to its high-risk clients and transactions.   24  Standard Chartered Bank  Singapore was   fined SGD 5.2  million by the Monetary  Authority of Singapore (MAS)  for AML failures, inadequate systems in place for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions,   inadequate transaction monitoring systems in place to detect suspicious  transactions, and inadequate  customer due diligence  measures in place, particularly  in relation to its high-risk clients and transactions.   27  DBS Bank   Singapore was  fined SGD 5.2 million by  the Monetary Authority of  Singapore (MAS)   for AML failures, inadequate systems for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions,  inadequate transaction monitoring systems in place to  detect suspicious transactions,  and inadequate customer due diligence measures in  place, particularly in relation  to its high-risk clients and  transactions. DBS Bank  Singapore will be required to enhance its transaction  monitoring systems, improve  its customer due diligence  measures, ensure that its AML  systems are compliant with  MAS regulations, appoint  an independent assessor to review its AML systems  and processes, and submit  regular reports to the MAS on its progress in addressing the  identified deficiencies.   25  Maybank   Singapore was  fined SGD 2.4 million by  the MAS for AML failures,  inadequate systems in place for identifying and reporting suspicious transactions,  inadequate customer due  diligence measures, and  inadequate transaction monitoring systems in place to  detect suspicious transactions,  particularly those related to its correspondent banking  activities. In addition to fines,  Maybank Singapore has also agreed to implement a number of remedial measures to improve its AML systems and processes.   26
# Page 17
THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT 17  United Kingdom  The United Kingdom’s approach to Anti-Money  Laundering (AML) regulations is measured by and follows the guidelines set out by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).  The UK government’s approach to cryptocurrency regulations has been moderate. Currently, the UK has no specific cryptocurrency laws; however,  cryptocurrencies are not considered legal tender  and crypto exchanges are mandated to have  registration requirements for every user. The UK government is seeking consultation on bringing  certain cryptocurrencies under the scope of financial  promotions regulation and continues to consider a broader regulatory approach to crypto assets. The HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has issued  a brief on the tax treatment of cryptocurrencies, stating that their ‘unique identity’ means they can’t be compared to conventional investments or payments, and their ‘taxability’ depends on the activities and parties involved. Overall, the UK’s approach to AML regulations is in line with the EU’s regulations and guidelines in the short term, but may diverge in the  future.  Discussion of the challenges and trends in the UK AML landscape  The United Kingdom has a few challenges and trends that have emerged in the AML landscape in recent years. One major challenge is the increase in cybercrime and the use of virtual assets for money laundering. This has led to a need for more robust regulations and oversight of virtual asset service providers. We have also seen the rise of professional money  launderers who use complex legal structures such as  shell companies and trusts to hide illicit funds. This has led regulators to push for increased transparency in  beneficial ownership. Additionally, the UK has seen an increase in cross-border financial crime, particularly in relation to bribery and corruption, which has prompted a need for more effective international cooperation and  information sharing. While the UK government is taking steps to address these challenges and trends by implementing stricter regulations and increasing resources for enforcement  agencies, it will take time to determine the effectiveness  of these measures.
# Page 18
18 THE 2023 REGWATCH REPORT  The UK government has an overarching view of AML policy that focuses on the prevention of money laundering  and terrorist financing—putting in place a series of measures to combat these crimes and to protect the integrity of the financial system. The UK’s approach to AML regulation is based on the principle of risk-based supervision,  which focuses on the areas of highest risk.  The main government agencies involved in AML regulation and enforcement in the UK are:  Government agencies, priorities, and initiatives  The Financial Conduct  Authority (FCA)  The FCA is responsible for  supervising financial institutions  to ensure they comply with  AML regulations, and for taking  enforcement action against those that fail to do so.  The National Crime Agency  (NCA)  The NCA is responsible for investigating and disrupting money laundering and terrorist  financing activities.  Both agencies work closely with  other government departments, such as the Home Office and HM Revenue & Customs, as well as  with international partners to combat these crimes. The FCA  and NCA have prioritized the fight against money laundering, terrorist financing and fraud,  as well as the protection of vulnerable people. They focus on the use of technology and data analysis to detect and  prevent money laundering,  as well as on the use of intelligence-led operations to target high-risk individuals and  organizations.
